item.title: SCP-3164:
item.content:encoded:
Downvoted for the test proposal with children, because the reason for proposing the test in the first place was not explicitly and compellingly identified. It felt like an immersion-breaking LOLFoundation moment. Note that I see absolutely nothing wrong with the concept of an amoral Foundation that uses children as D-class fodder, but it should be clear what additional information or benefit the Foundation hopes to gain from the experiment or procedure. Otherwise it feels like a lame joke.

Also, this doesn't make sense:

Since this date, no new active phases have been observed, despite the presence of individuals overnight.

The site's being monitored, contained, and systematically tested by the Foundation, but there's no experiment log for these individuals who were present overnight? What, did these individuals slip past Foundation security and spend the night while the researchers took a holiday? I'm sorry to say, it honestly feels like the author got sick of writing and gave up.

item.title: SCP-3162:
item.content:encoded:
Hmm.

Under no circumstances are Foundation personnel to use information gleaned from archival SCP-3162 entries to guide or influence their interpersonal relationships.

As phrased, compliance after exposure to archival entries seems almost literally impossible (the ready availability of amnestics in SCP-world is the only reason for "almost"). Perhaps this could be rephrased to indicate (a) limitations on accessing archival entries, or (b) precisely what personnel should do if they do encounter information that would influence their interpersonal relationships.

item.title: SCP-3160:
item.content:encoded:
Delightful. (Never thought I'd say that about an insect scip.) This reminds me of various Series I scips, ones that don't offer much explicit insight into how the information in the article was obtained or deduced. The document just presents a weird thing in the universe that is somehow thoroughly understood by the Foundation; the scip's strength is the elegant simplicity and quirky cleverness of its weird idea.

I think that's a great approach even when aiming to fulfill modern standards. Arguably, a realistic containment procedures writeup is unlikely to contain the addenda and experiment logs that a lot of modern SCPs rely on to tell their story (because a realistic containment procedures writeup wouldn't be trying to tell a story).

item.title: SCP-3159:
item.content:encoded:
I see a couple other people have already commented that this shouldn't be "Safe" by modern definitions of object classes. This one doesn't even feel like a close call to me, but I am still learning the system, so I'm open to explanations.

If you're reading this comment and you believe Safe *is* the correct designation, can you please reply to me and explain why? You don't have to be the scip's author; I'll hear anybody out. (For the record, I personally do not mind if you "necro" in order to reply to this question. I'm not a mod, I'm just an ordinary reader; please don't break site rules for my sake; however, I have seen mods comment elsewhere that necro replies can be acceptable when they further a conversation productively.)
